messages:
alex: Thinking out loud — we need a concrete NVTX policy for the runtime. My current pain: per-request spans are great, but adding per-kernel ranges for everything blows up nsys timelines and impacts throughput. Looking for conventions and a low-overhead approach.

tasha: Agree. Tradeoff = visibility vs overhead. My rule-of-thumb: keep a single request-level span + a few coarse-grained phases (decode, kv-cache, kernel-dispatch). Only enable kernel-level ranges when doing focused perf debugging.

jordan: Data point from last week's nsys runs: enabling NVTX ranges around every cuLaunchKernel (hot path) reduced steady-state throughput ~6–9% on p4d tests (batch=8, seq=1024). The timeline is great for root-cause but too noisy for normal deployments.

sophie: Can we do sampling? e.g., sample 1/100 requests with full kernel ranges and otherwise only high-level spans? That would keep avg overhead low but give us examples.

alex: Sampling is a good idea. Implementation sketch: add runtime-level sampling that flips a per-request flag and only creates fine-grained NVTX ranges if flag is set. Also expose env like REDWOOD_NVTX=off|high|sampled.

jordan: +1. Also we should use RAII wrappers so instrumentation is cheap to call and easy to scope. Example we used: 
```cpp
struct NvtxRange {
  NvtxRange(const char* name) { nvtxRangePushA(name); }
  ~NvtxRange() { nvtxRangePop(); }
};

// usage
if (should_trace) { NvtxRange r("req:1234:kv_lookup"); /* body */ }
```
This keeps the call site compact.

tasha: On naming: prefer short, structured names so they fit in timeline UI. Suggested pattern: 
`req:<id>|phase:<name>|m:<model_short>|s:<seq>`
Examples: `req:42|phase:kv|m:gptj8k|s:128` or for kernel spans `req:42|k:attn_fwd`
Keep it ascii-only, no spaces.

sophie: For kernel-level debugging we should also add an anchor tag with kernel id + op signature so we can map `cuLaunchKernel` hotspots to our kernel source. e.g., include kernel hex or a short hashed sig: `k:attn_fwd#0x7a3`

alex: Important: avoid creating NVTX ranges around extremely short repeated ops (e.g., small elementwise kernels called thousands of times). Instead aggregate them: `req:42|phase:decode-batch` that wraps a group of kernels.

jordan: KV cache behavior: prefer metrics/telemetry for hit/miss counts (prom counters) and only add NVTX span around cache lookup when doing an end-to-end trace. Dense NVTXs for each lookup were the main source of overhead in last run.

infra-bot: perf-run uploaded: https://internal.perf/runs/17719 (nsys capture with kernel names annotated) :eyes:

alex: A few practical rules we should adopt for the runtime codebase: 
1) Always: top-level request span `req:<id>|lifecycle`. Cheap and on by default.
2) Default: coarse phases `kv`, `batching`, `dispatch`, `decode`. On by default, low frequency.
3) Opt-in: per-kernel ranges behind `REDWOOD_NVTX=kernel` or sampling. Not enabled in prod builds.
4) Implementation: single RAII helper in runtime_core with a fast-path that checks a thread-local `trace_enabled` bool before calling NVTX.
5) Build: compile-time switch for nvtx to remove calls in static builds (zero overhead).

tasha: Also: store a small per-request GUID in TLS so names don't get huge. Eg `req:0x1a2b`. UI can map GUID -> user-friendly id in post-processing.

sophie: For perf tickets: add a checklist to include nsys capture + perfetto with the same nvtx naming so we can correlate. Also include a short 'how-to' in eng-runtime README with the env vars and example capture commands.

jordan: One additional note: when we map kernel names in nsys we rely on CUPTI/kernel_name heuristics. Adding a tiny NVTX annotation right before dispatch with a canonical kernel short name makes mapping 100x simpler.

alex: OK action items: 
- @tasha to PR RAII helper + env var and default top-level spans.
- @jordan to add sampling logic + test harness and run perf matrix.
- @sophie to add README snippet and update perf run checklist.
- infra-bot: pin the nsys capture link into the perf ticket.

Any objections?

tasha: No objections. I'll start the PR today. :+1:

sophie: I'll draft the README.

jordan: I'll run a quick A/B to measure sampling rate vs visibility.

alex: Great. We'll revisit after the PRs land and once we have a clean sampled nsys capture. Thanks all. :rocket:
